chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Ibrahim ibn Maymoun, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Al-Fitra is that you give it before you go out to the Eid, so it is Fitra; and if it was after you go out to the Eid, so it is charity.'

key_terms.الْعِيدِ: Eid (the festival prayer, specifically Eid al-Fitr in this context)
key_terms.الْفِطْرَةُ: Fitra (the obligatory alms-tax paid on Eid al-Fitr)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Fitra and Sadaqah based on the time of payment?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the juridical status of alms by linking the timing of payment to the Eid prayer, establishing that pre-prayer distribution fulfills the obligatory Fitra while post-prayer giving remains voluntary Sadaqah. This distinction underscores the ritual significance of synchronizing financial purification with the communal worship of Eid, a practice deeply rooted in Shia fiqh to ensure the validity of the obligatory duty before engaging in celebratory gatherings.
